ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Madam C. J. Walker — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for viral gastroenteritis with sick-day rules

text.paragraph: Vomiting and diarrhea since the day before yesterday. [S]

Madam Walker called this morning and was seen the same day. She came home two days ago from a sales convention where several agents had a stomach illness. That night she began vomiting, four times by morning, with six loose watery stools over the next day and cramping around the navel. The vomiting stopped yesterday afternoon; she is keeping down sips of broth and an oral rehydration drink, and the diarrhea has slowed to two stools today. No blood in the stool and no fever above 37.5 °C. She feels light-headed when she stands quickly. Following the sick-day card in her bag, she has not taken losartan or empagliflozin since the vomiting began; she took nothing for pain. She has kept taking atorvastatin. She is passing less urine than usual. [S]

list.item:
Viral gastroenteritis with mild volume depletion (A08.4). Probable viral gastroenteritis, with similar illness among people she was with. Vomiting has stopped and she can drink. Mild volume depletion: postural rise in pulse, dry mouth, less urine. No blood in the stool, high fever or severe pain, so stool tests and antibiotics are not needed. Creatinine 1.46 mg/dL (eGFR 44), up from 1.29 on treatment: a rise of 0.17 mg/dL, below the threshold for acute kidney injury, from volume loss. Potassium 4.9 and bicarbonate 21 mmol/L, glucose 88 mg/dL. [S]
Oral rehydration solution, small amounts often, at least 2 to 3 liters a day until urine is pale.
Ondansetron 4 mg dissolved on the tongue every 8 hours as needed, for up to two days.
Bland food as she feels able.
Hand washing and separate towels at home.

Chronic kidney disease G3a A2, sick-day rules (N18.31). She applied her sick-day rules correctly. With volume loss, losartan and empagliflozin can lower kidney blood flow further, and empagliflozin adds to fluid loss; holding both is right. Atorvastatin can continue. [S]
Keep holding losartan and empagliflozin until she has eaten and drunk normally for 24 hours, then restart both at the usual doses.
No ibuprofen or naproxen; acetaminophen if needed.
Metabolic panel within a week.
Go to the emergency department for vomiting that returns and stops her drinking, fainting, no urine for 12 hours, or blood in the stool.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease (2024)

Follow-up: Nurse phone call tomorrow. Metabolic panel within a week; eleven-week review in two weeks as booked. Emergency care for vomiting that stops her drinking, fainting, no urine for 12 hours, or blood in the stool. Next scheduled visit 1917-04-27: eleven-week review: home readings on maximum losartan, urine albumin, kidney function after a recent gastroenteritis, lipids on atorvastatin. [S]
